_doc: Barter values (per item) and the traders at Riverside. Traders sell at full value and buy at 'buyRate'. Stock lists: [item, quantity on hand]; stock refills every in-game day.

general.name: Hanne Voss
general.title: General goods
general.greeting: Food, water, clothes, batteries. Cash is dead — I trade in goods. Cigarettes and watches always welcome.

gunsmith.name: Emil Brandt
gunsmith.title: Gunsmith
gunsmith.greeting: Guns, rounds and parts. Bring me a rifle that's falling apart and I'll make it shoot straight again — for a price.

medic.name: Dr. Aleksa Moreau
medic.title: Medic
medic.greeting: Sit down. If you're bleeding, I'll stitch you; if you're not, I'll sell you what you need so you can do it yourself next time.

builder.name: Jonas Kell
builder.title: Builder
builder.greeting: Planks, nails, sheet metal, tools. Everything you need for a wall that stops bullets. Or most of them.

quartermaster.name: Sgt. Radek Hollis
quartermaster.title: Quartermaster
quartermaster.greeting: The Guard pays for work. Bring what's on the board and you'll be paid in kind. I also have a little surplus kit, if you've got something to trade.

elder.name: Ida Lindqvist
elder.title: Settlement elder
elder.greeting: Welcome to Riverside. Keep your weapon low inside the walls and you'll find us fair. People pass through here all day — I hear a great deal.

civilianLines: Wolves hit the farms east of here last week. Took everything that wasn't nailed down.
The water plant? Mercenaries hold it now. They charge for every litre.
If you're heading north, stay off the highway near the checkpoint. The Security Forces shoot first.
My brother went to Old Vesper for medicine. That was nine days ago.
Trade with Hanne if you need food. She's fair, mostly.
Emil can fix anything that fires. Bring him the parts and he'll do it cheaper.
Night patrols see lights moving up on Redstone Ridge. Nobody goes up there to check.
The Guard pays for scrap. Sergeant Hollis keeps a list at the quartermaster's stall.
Build somewhere with a view, and lock your crates. People talk about who has what.
I used to drive buses on this road. Now I grow potatoes behind the hall.
